SV-10002.title: Global Search: a customer cannot be found by their postcode
SV-10002.description: A customer's postcode is on their record and the search box ignores it. Anyone who knows roughly where a customer is - which is how people tell two similar company names apart - has no way to get to them from the search box. On the version people use today, typing the postcode brings the customer straight back.
steps: Open Customers, open any customer, and read the postcode on their record. On the test branch use ZZAUTOTEST Bridgeport Hauling, whose postcode is 44872-9931.
Click the search box at the top of the screen (or press Ctrl and K together).
Type that postcode exactly as it appears on the record.
Wait for the results and read the Customers group.
current: Nothing comes back at all. The panel reads "No results for 44872-9931" and every group shows a count of zero.
The same customer is returned immediately if their name is typed instead, so the record is there and the search box is working.
expected: The customer whose postcode was typed is returned, under the Customers group.
This is what the version people use today does.
SV-10002.shot_caption: The same postcode typed into both versions. Above, the live product returns the customer. Below, the new version returns nothing.
SV-10002.sources: The expected behaviour comes from the version of the product that is live today, where the postcode is part of what a customer can be found by. It was typed into the live product on 15 September 2026 and the customer came back; the picture above is that search. Nothing else is being relied on.
